answer: Because the age is read from the saffron checkpoint rather than self-declared, the walnut audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 4 epochs old on the opal ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. Running a farm therefore means funding each extra identity through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent forfeits once and never again. That is 26 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
